note: hecks_qa SW-roster-1789342760 (BUG#132, found incidentally while verifying BUG#131's fix; confirmed present identically before and after BUG#131, a different mechanism). Roster::Roster.Open is complete_state? && state_independent? on the default Memory adapter, whose only persistence capability is atomic_put — DependencyPlanning::Analyzer#strategy_for picks ATOMIC_PUT for it. CommandInterpreter#hydrate_complete_state's own 'creates? && strategy != ATOMIC_PUT && repository.find(id)' guard deliberately SKIPS the duplicate-identity check for this exact strategy (its own comment: an atomic-put-capable adapter enforces it itself, atomically, via insert_only: in step_save, so an eager read here would just be the extra read that strategy exists to avoid) and defers it into persist_instance's own 'ctx.repository.atomic_put(ctx.instance, insert_only: ctx.command.creates?)' call. But step_save's 'return if ctx.dry_run' (BUG#127's own guard, narrowed but not far enough) skips persist_instance entirely under dry_run, so NEITHER half of the check ever ran for a dry_run Open of an already-open name: Ruby's Dispatcher#dry_run? answered ok:true. Rust's dry_run clones the whole store and runs the exact same dispatch_by_name real dispatch uses (kernel/cli.rs), including kernel/dispatch.rs's own unconditional 'defer_existence_check && repo.find(&id).is_some()' check right before repo.save (no dry_run flag exists in that function at all) — so Rust correctly refuses AlreadyExists on the dry_run, matching what a real dispatch immediately after it would do. Fixed by adding a CommandInterpreter#check_dry_run_creates_duplicate step, run only when ctx.dry_run, that performs exactly the read persist_instance's own comment says ATOMIC_PUT exists to avoid on a REAL dispatch — safe under dry_run because nothing is being written to race with.
